relatedSnapshot.title: Workspace deletion is switched off platform-wide, leaving a sole owner with no self-serve way to delete workspace or account
relatedSnapshot.description:
Support/Product follow-up from the Intercom intake (second question on the same conversation).

Intercom source: <url:app.intercom.com>
Conversation context: The customer says his workspace is not deleted, asks for further payments to be cancelled, and wants the account deleted. He told the agent the workspace still exists. Investigator was asked to check whether there is a bug deleting the workspace, because the client cannot delete it.

Finding (workspace deletion is switched off platform-wide, not failing):

* packages/db/src/types/organization-lifecycle.ts sets ORGANIZATION_SOFT_DELETE_ROLLOUT_ENABLED = false. That is a compile-time constant, so it is off for every environment and every user.
* Every deletion entry point is gated on it: the owner-facing Danger Zone card (apps/web/components/organization/delete-organization-card.tsx) returns null and is only rendered when the flag is true on the General settings page; the tRPC organizations.deleteOrganization returns PRECONDITION_FAILED "Workspace deletion is temporarily unavailable."; the admin deleteById and deleteManyById mutations do the same; and the public API DELETE /workspaces/{id} returns 409 conflict. The API description documents this state as "staged and currently unavailable".
* Consequence for this customer: he is the only active member and sole owner of one active workspace, so the account-deletion guard (apps/web/lib/auth/delete-account.ts, getOwnedActiveWorkspacesForAccountDeletion / assertAccountDeletionAllowedForUser) blocks deleting his personal account until another owner is added or the workspace is deleted. The blocking dialog in apps/web/components/user/delete-account-card.tsx offers a "Delete workspace" button that links to the workspace General settings page, where the delete card is not rendered. So both self-serve exits lead nowhere.
* The public help article "General Settings" and the FAQ on cancelling a workspace still instruct customers to use Settings - General - Danger Zone - Delete Workspace, which no longer exists in the product.

Blast radius (current query, 17 Sep 2026): 9,735 active workspaces have no self-serve delete control while the flag is off, and 8,737 of them have exactly one owner member, so those accounts also cannot be deleted by their owner.

Proposed human action: (1) unblock this customer, since he has no self-serve path to remove himself; (2) decide whether the deletion rollout is enabled now, or whether the account-deletion dialog and the public help articles should stop pointing at a disabled control. This is a product/limitation finding, not a runtime failure, so it is filed for a human decision rather than as engineering root-cause work.

relatedSnapshot.title: Consolidate duplicate zod versions in the workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
The monorepo currently resolves more than one `zod` version (e.g. `apps/web` on zod 4.x while `apps/api` has pulled zod 3.x). Because the class identity differs across copies, `error.cause instanceof ZodError` is unreliable in tests: a `ZodError` thrown by a router is not identity-equal to any single imported `ZodError`.

Workaround in place: `apps/web/tests/support/zod-helpers.ts` (`getZodIssues`) inspects `cause.issues` structurally instead of using `instanceof`. This is version-agnostic but is a symptom, not a fix.

### Ask

* Name 19 `zod` to a single workspace version (pin/override so all packages resolve one copy).
* Once deduped, tests can assert `instanceof ZodError` directly and the structural helper can be simplified or removed.

### Context

Surfaced during review of PR #5781 (ENG-11996) — <url:github.com>

relatedSnapshot.title: Prevent duplicate workspace setup on repeated onboarding runs
relatedSnapshot.description: Users can reset onboarding multiple times and repeat the workspace setup process. This may create duplicate workspaces and unnecessary costs. Consider preventing duplicates (e.g., enforce a unique workspaceId based on the user slug) so reruns fail gracefully if a workspace already exists.
